blocks.text: What an AI assistant for lawyers on Mac does

An AI assistant for lawyers on Mac works alongside the apps you already use. It does not replace Word, Outlook or your document system. It listens while you hold a shortcut, looks at what is on your screen and answers. That is the core of it. The rest is detail about what it can and cannot do.

Lazur works this way. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and it answers out loud. Ask where something is and it draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. It does not click for you. You keep control of the document, the email and the send button.
Where a lawyer's working hours go

The best recent number comes from Bloomberg Law's 2024 Attorney Workload and Hours survey. Attorneys worked about 48 hours a week in 2024, and billed 36 of those hours. The survey drew 1,054 responses, fielded from January 8 to 27, 2025. The figures here come from legal.io's summary, not the full report, so check the full report before you quote them.

The same survey found attorneys spent two of every eight working hours on administrative duties, on average. That is one quarter of the day. The survey does not say how those hours split between email, filing and billing. Do not read more into it than that.

An older source gives a bigger share. Clio's 2017 Legal Trends Report, as reported by National Jurist, put administrative tasks at 48 percent of the average lawyer's day. Billable utilization was 29 percent, about 2.3 billable hours in an eight-hour day. That data is from 2017. Sources describe the 48 percent figure in different ways, so use it as a pattern, not as your number.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics counts about 863,700 lawyer jobs in 2025, and projects 5 percent employment growth from 2025 to 2035. BLS describes the core work as preparing and filing documents such as lawsuits, contracts and wills, plus legal research and client communication. It does not measure computer time, or how much of that work happens on a screen.
Finding a clause in a long document in Word

Start with the document open in Word for Mac. Edit > Find > Find (⌘F) locates a word. It cannot tell you what a clause means or whether it is the one you need. That gap is where an AI assistant helps. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where the termination clause is. Lazur looks at the page on screen, finds the section and circles it with a label.

Lazur works from the screen, so the section has to be visible. If the clause sits on another page, scroll there first, then ask. Three questions work well on a services agreement. Ask where the indemnity cap is. Ask which section sets the notice period. Ask what the governing law clause says.

items: Open the agreement in Word and scroll to the page you think holds the clause.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and say where the termination clause is.
Read the circle and the label, then read the clause yourself.
Ask a follow-up, such as whether the notice period counts business days.
Check the answer against the text before you rely on it.

blocks.text: If you are comparing two versions, the job changes. Use Review > Compare in Word, then ask about the differences you find. The redlining steps are in [how to compare two Word documents on a Mac](/for/lawyers/problems/compare-two-word-documents-on-mac). For more on Word, see [Microsoft Word for lawyers on Mac](/for/lawyers/word).
Summarizing an agreement without losing the exceptions

Summaries save the most time, and they carry the most risk. Open the page, hold ⌥ ⌘ and say sum up this page. Lazur reads what is on screen and gives you the gist out loud. For a dense section, ask for what matters to you, such as who pays, what the deadline is and what happens on breach.

A summary is a starting point, not a reading. Lazur sees only what is on your screen. A long agreement will not fit on one screen, so summarize one section at a time. Keep a note of which section each summary came from.

The mistake to avoid is reading a summary and treating it as the clause. Exceptions, carve-outs and defined terms live in the detail. A summary often drops them. Use the summary to find the section, then read the section in full.

blocks.title: Test it on a known clause
blocks.text: Pick a clause you already know well and ask for a summary. If the answer misses a carve-out you know is there, you have learned the limit of the tool before a matter depends on it.
Drafting email in Outlook for lawyers on Mac

Most legal email has a shape. A status update to a client. A request for an extension. A reply that says the answer is coming. Hold ⌥ ⌘ in Outlook and ask for a status update on the discovery schedule. Lazur drafts it in Outlook for you to edit. Read the draft, check the dates and change the tone to fit the relationship.

Dictation handles the rest of the message. Click into the body, hold fn and speak. Dictation writes clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Add snippets for the sentences you type every week. Add case names and party names to the personal dictionary before a long day.

Outlook 2024 for Mac also helps after you hit send. Microsoft lists scheduled send, delay delivery, Undo Send and Focused Inbox among its new features. Scheduled send and delay delivery work only with cloud-based accounts. If your firm runs its own mail server, check whether those options apply before you schedule a client message.

items: Scheduled send: queue a message for a later time. Cloud accounts only.
Delay delivery: hold a message on its own or by rule. Cloud accounts only.
Undo Send: recall a message for a short time after you send it.
Focused Inbox and custom swipe gestures: sort the noise, then act faster.

blocks.text: For filing and search tips in the same app, see [Outlook for lawyers on Mac](/for/lawyers/outlook).

blocks.title: Schedule with a second look
blocks.text: Schedule client updates for the start of the day. Then read them once more before they go out.
Deadlines, reminders and timers during a busy day

Deadlines are the easiest thing to lose in a busy day. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and say remind me of the filing deadline Monday at 9. Lazur adds a reminder in Apple Reminders. Calendar events and timers work the same way. Say timer for 6 minutes, billing and Lazur starts one in the notch.

A reminder is not a docket. Court deadlines depend on the court's rules, the type of filing and the method of service. Confirm each date against the rules and your firm's docketing system. Use Lazur to remind you to check, not to work out the date.
The common mistake is a voice reminder set from a date nobody checked. A reminder on a wrong date is still a wrong date, now with a sound.

blocks.title: Check, do not calculate
blocks.text: Use reminders for the check, not the calculation. A missed deadline cannot be fixed by a chime.
Research in Chrome with a voice assistant

A lot of legal research starts in a browser. Lazur runs research in its own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It works through sources, then comes back with a summary and a report. Its tabs are separate from the ones you have open.

Court filing sites and research databases often need a login and a fee. Check each site's terms before you point a research job at it. Some sites limit automated access, and a summary of the results does not change those terms. Read the site first.

Use research jobs for the broad sweep. Use your own judgment for the final read. Verify every case citation at the source before it goes into a brief. A summary can name a case that does not say what the summary claims. More on the browser side is in [Chrome for lawyers on Mac](/for/lawyers/chrome).
Dictation for file notes and memos on Mac
Many lawyers think faster out loud. Hold fn in any app and speak. Dictation writes clean, formatted text at the cursor. It is included with Lazur, and it is unlimited on both the Pro and Power plans.

Use it for the first draft of a file note, a memo outline or a summary of a call. Then edit by hand. Dictation gets names wrong unless you teach it. Add party names, case names and local terms to the personal dictionary before a long session.

Dictation works best in a quiet room. Speak clearly, pause at the end of each sentence and check the first paragraph before you go on. Try the [speaking versus typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test) on a real file note.

blocks.title: Mind who can hear
blocks.text: Do not dictate privileged material in a shared office. Anyone nearby can hear it, and the text is only as private as the room.
Office for Mac changes that can stop editing

This is the part most guides skip. Microsoft says that from July 13, 2026, Microsoft 365 subscribers on Mac, and people with one-time Office 2021 or 2019 on Mac, may get a reduced mode. In that mode, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and OneNote can open and print files. They cannot edit, save or create new files.

Read the same guide, then ask IT which version the firm uses

Confirm the status with Microsoft before a filing day
blocks.caption: Based on Microsoft's known-issues page for Word for Mac. Check the guide for exact affected versions.

blocks.text: Updates have a second requirement. Since the September 2025 update, version 16.101, Microsoft 365 and Office for Mac updates need macOS Sonoma 14 or later. Older macOS versions can still run Office. They get no further updates, including security updates. That is a question for your firm's IT team, not only for you.

Check the latest release, too. Version 16.114.3, released October 27, 2026, lists Outlook and Word only as quality and performance improvements, with no new features. Do not expect a new feature to solve a licensing problem.

blocks.title: Check the version first
blocks.text: Since July 13, 2026, check which Office version each Mac runs. A reduced mode on the morning of a filing is a bad start.
Client data, privilege and your firm's rules

Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. When you hold it, the audio and one screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you. Those are not stored, and they are never used to train AI models. That is how it works. Whether it fits your matter is a separate question.

Your duty runs to your client and to your firm's policy. Many firms set rules on which AI tools can see client material, on which matters, and what can go into a document. Read the written policy first. If it is silent, ask before you use an AI tool on a live matter.
Lazur makes no compliance claims for legal practice, and this page makes none either. Your firm decides what fits. Your bar's rules and your client agreements may add to that.

items: Read your firm's written policy on AI tools and client data.
Confirm the matter allows an outside AI provider to see its documents.
Close windows and tabs you do not need on screen.
Know that Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, on the Mac.
Ask your IT or risk team if the policy does not answer your question.

blocks.title: Policy first, shortcut second
blocks.text: Holding ⌥ ⌘ over a privileged document is a choice. Your firm's policy decides whether you should make it.
Mistakes lawyers make with an AI assistant on Mac

items: Treating a summary as the clause. Read the section before you rely on it.
Asking about a section that is off screen. Scroll to it first.
Trusting a voice reminder set from a date you have not checked.
Expecting Lazur to operate your apps. It points, explains and drafts. You do the clicking and the sending.
Scheduling client email on an account that does not support scheduled send.
Dictating names without adding them to the personal dictionary.

faq.question: Is Lazur an AI assistant for lawyers on Mac that works in Word?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works on top of Word on the Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about what is on screen, and it answers out loud. It does not edit or save the document for you. It points, explains and drafts text you can edit.

faq.question: Is Lazur approved for legal work?
faq.answer: Lazur makes no compliance claims for legal practice, and this page makes none either. Check your firm's policy on AI tools and client data before you use it on a matter. Ask your IT or risk team if the policy is unclear.

faq.question: Does Lazur send my documents to AI providers?
faq.answer: When you hold the shortcut, the audio and one screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you. They are not stored, and they are never used to train AI models. Read your firm's rules to decide if that fits the matter.

faq.question: Is Lazur always listening or watching my screen?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons, file or send email for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. Ask how to do something and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

faq.question: Can Lazur tell me the exact filing deadline?
faq.answer: Do not rely on it for that. Court deadlines depend on the court's rules, the filing type and how the document is served. Confirm the date against the rules and your docketing system. Lazur can remind you to check.

faq.question: Does Outlook scheduled send work with every account?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Microsoft says scheduled send and delay delivery only work with cloud-based accounts. Check which account the matter uses before you rely on either feature.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: How much does Lazur cost for a lawyer?
faq.answer: There is a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. It starts when you first open the app. Pro is $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually, with 150 AI actions. Power is $120 a month, or $96 a month billed annually, with 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both.
